title: microbatch orchestration and KV occupancy cleanup
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Reduce tail latency and memory churn by consolidating the microbatch coordinator, introducing an occupancy-aware KV cache compaction policy, and removing legacy timers in the scheduler.

Problem: Over time we've accumulated multiple ad-hoc microbatch pathways (legacy timer-driven enqueues, opportunistic merge path, and a newer epochal coordinator). These layers interact poorly under bursty traffic: the coordinator over-allocates batch slots, the KV cache keeps fragmented session regions, and the scheduler timers induce jitter. The result is increased p99 latency, elevated peak memory usage, and frequent GC pauses on certain node types.

Goal: Provide a single microbatch orchestration path that: 1) deterministically merges compatible requests within SLOs; 2) exposes an occupancy metric to the KV cache so eviction/compaction targets hot vs. cold session regions; and 3) removes legacy timer-heartbeat code paths to reduce jitter. Deliverables include a coordinator refactor, a KV occupancy compaction policy, and scheduler cleanup with observable fallbacks.

Approach:
- Implement a Microbatch Coordinator (MBC) that unifies enqueue sources. MBC will accept tokens from the ingress, prefer coalescing by model&seqlen fingerprint, and emit microbatches respecting a configurable latency budget.
- Add an occupancy map to the KV store: per-shard lightweight counters that track active slot references and delta-decay over time. Use this signal to drive compaction rather than purely LRU TTLs.
- Replace legacy timer-driven enqueue with an adaptive poll in the coordinator that backs off under high contention; remove the old timer shim once coordinator proves >=99% path coverage in canary.
- Provide observability: microbatch-size histogram, occupancy heatmap (per-shard), compaction events, and scheduler jitter metric.

Milestones:
- Week 1: design doc + interface RFC and perf targets (latency, memory).
- Week 2: implement coordinator core + unit tests; KV occupancy map prototype.
- Week 3: integrate compaction policy + e2e perf harness; start canary on low-traffic pool.
- Week 4: rollback/canary analysis, address regressions, promote to staged rollout.

Acceptance Criteria:
- p99 token latency reduced by >=10% on targeted workloads vs baseline (controlled A/B).
- Peak memory per GPU host reduced by >=8% under synthetic high-surge test.
- Coordinator path handles >=99% of enqueues in canary region with no increase in error rate.
- Compaction events produce measurable eviction of cold session regions without harming hot-session latency.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: occupancy counters add write amplification to KV store. Mitigation: use batched and sampled increments, and decay counters on read paths only.
- Risk: coordinator incorrectly merges requests that should be isolated (security/tenant boundaries). Mitigation: fingerprinting includes tenant and request-level isolation tokens; cross-tenant merging is disallowed.

Testing Plan: unit tests for MBC state machine, KV occupancy invariants, fuzz tests for merge correctness, and a full-scale perf test (10x baseline QPS) in staging. Metrics gated before rollout.

Notes & Links: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Microbatch+Coordinator+RFC; perf dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/mbc-staging; initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/1982
